question: Do prior price dips and low proximity predict positive same-day open-to-close returns?
scope: Primary-source literature review and hypotheses; no trading recommendation or production-model change.
retrieval_note: web__run returned 404. Sources retrieved directly from author/university/institution/publisher URLs using urllib; Crossref/OpenAlex used for discovery and bibliographic confirmation. This was selective literature retrieval, not a comprehensive current search. Five primary PDFs inspected; two additional studies reviewed at publisher-abstract level only.
key_conclusion: Temporary selling pressure is a plausible reversal mechanism, but the user’s exact two-down-days + 52-week-low + unrebounded-at-entry conjunction remains an unvalidated intraday hypothesis. Separating information-driven decline, session timing, rebound already consumed, trend and execution costs is essential.
lookahead_rules: Historical return/range/volume/trend features stop at t−1.
Current open is observable only after it occurs; a decision based on that price must use an executable subsequent entry or explicitly documented opening-auction assumption.
A signal using the first 5/15/30 minutes requires a delayed-entry label, not official-open-to-close.
Current-day low/high/volume and hindsight article sentiment must not enter morning features.

sources.title: A tug of war: Overnight versus intraday expected returns
sources.verified_content: Published PDF, author-hosted at LSE; relevant abstract, methods, tables and discussion read.
sources.sample: Core US CRSP/Compustat/TAQ sample 1993–2013; robustness includes nine large non-US equity markets.
sources.horizon: Monthly sorting signals and subsequent monthly aggregates of daily overnight and intraday returns. Main open proxy is 9:30–10:00 VWAP, with robustness to actual opening prices and bid-ask midpoint.
findings: Past overnight returns predict subsequent overnight continuation and intraday reversal; past intraday returns predict subsequent intraday continuation and overnight reversal.
The conventional short-term reversal premium and four momentum-strategy premia accrue overnight in their decomposition; close-to-close success cannot be assumed to survive an open-to-close strategy.
limitations: This is not a test of two down days followed by one open-to-close trade.
Published long-short gross portfolio alphas do not establish the user’s executable long-only net edge; 30-minute VWAP is not the opening auction.
feature_hypotheses: Separate lagged overnight from lagged session losses; retain longer session-specific history rather than aggregating everything into close-to-close return.
Measure how much of the prior selloff has already rebounded by the intended entry.

sources.title: Decomposing Short-Term Return Reversal
sources.publication: Federal Reserve Bank of New York Staff Report 513, September 2011 (version actually reviewed)
sources.verified_content: Primary institutional PDF; abstract, sample, strategy, decomposition and robustness discussion read.
sources.sample: January 1982–March 2009; non-penny stocks with sufficient analyst forecasts, relatively large/liquid and about 75% of US equity capitalization.
sources.horizon: Previous-month signals and following-month returns; original analysis uses I/B/E/S-month timing, with calendar-month robustness.
findings: Within-industry residual price changes unexplained by cash-flow news drive reversal; industry momentum and underreaction to cash-flow news offset indiscriminate reversal.
Buying residual losers is associated with liquidity shocks; selling residual winners with sentiment.
The authors report midpoint-return robustness and explicitly estimate trading costs.
limitations: Their residual is not simply stock minus sector: expected returns and analyst forecast revisions also enter.
Monthly forecast revisions and monthly holding evidence do not validate a next-morning intraday rule.
A news flag is only an implementable approximation to this economic distinction, not a replication.
feature_hypotheses: Volatility-scaled idiosyncratic drawdown relative to market/sector, interacted with timestamped news or earnings shocks.

sources.title: Evaporating Liquidity
sources.verified_content: Primary NBER PDF; abstract, empirical construction, sample, quote controls and VIX discussion read.
sources.horizon: Daily close-to-close reversal portfolios averaging five sub-strategies using lagged returns from t−1 through t−5.
findings: Expected short-term reversal returns rise with VIX, consistent with compensation for supplying liquidity when intermediaries withdraw.
Both transaction-price and quote-midpoint returns are studied; quote data are available for Nasdaq stocks.
limitations: Transaction-price returns model a hypothetical liquidity supplier executing at the closing print; a market-order user pays execution costs.
This is close-to-close evidence, not a demonstrated next-open-to-close edge.
Market turmoil, execution frictions and institutional changes matter; high expected reversal is not a guarantee of a safe individual trade.
feature_hypotheses: Interact residual selloff with lagged market volatility and lagged liquidity/dollar-volume measures; evaluate net results by regime.

sources.title: The 52-Week High and Momentum Investing
sources.publication: Journal of Finance LIX(5), October 2004, pp.2145–2176
sources.verified_content: Published author-hosted PDF; abstract, interpretation, sample and strategy methodology read.
sources.horizon: Portfolios formed monthly using price relative to the preceding 12-month high; held six months. Regression tests skip one month to reduce bid-ask effects.
findings: Nearness to a 52-week high predicts stronger subsequent returns and accounts for much conventional momentum.
Their anchoring interpretation allows bad-news stocks far below prior highs to continue falling.
limitations: This is six-month momentum evidence, not evidence that buying today’s high beats today’s dip.
Far below a 52-week high is not equivalent to hitting a fresh 52-week low.
No automatic positive intraday effect of a fresh 52-week low is established here.
feature_hypotheses: Keep long-trend/high-proximity context alongside low-proximity and drawdown; test pullbacks within strength separately from continuing downtrends.

sources.title: Trading Volume and Serial Correlation in Stock Returns
sources.publication: NBER Working Paper 4193, October 1992; published Quarterly Journal of Economics 108(4), November 1993, pp. 905–939
sources.verified_content: NBER abstract and scanned primary PDF; pages 3–5 and 7–8 rendered locally and visually read because text extraction was blank.
sources.sample: Main CRSP NYSE/AMEX value-weighted index sample July 3, 1962–September 30, 1987; robustness through December 30, 1988, earlier index data, DJIA and 32 large stocks.
sources.horizon: Daily returns; regressions of the next day’s return on lagged return interacted with detrended volume. No overnight/session separation.
findings: Return autocorrelation declines as volume rises; in the model, high-volume declines are more consistent with noninformational selling pressure and subsequently higher expected returns.
limitations: Primarily aggregate-market evidence from an older market structure, not a modern stock-specific intraday entry test.
Volume can also accompany information events; this source does not justify treating every high-volume selloff as capitulation.
This is explanatory/statistical evidence, not an executable after-cost strategy estimate.
feature_hypotheses: Prior-day abnormal dollar volume × residual decline, conditioned on news and market regime.

sources.title: Paying Attention: Overnight Returns and the Hidden Cost of Buying at the Open
sources.publication: Journal of Financial and Quantitative Analysis 47(4), pp.715–741
sources.verified_content: Publisher abstract verified on Cambridge page and publisher-deposited Crossref abstract; full text not obtained.
sources.sample: Not verified from accessible abstract; do not state a sample period.
sources.horizon: Overnight returns versus the following trading day.
findings: Positive overnight returns followed by trading-day reversals are concentrated in stocks recently attracting retail attention.
The authors attribute this to relatively high opening prices and describe implicit buying-at-open costs beyond the effective half-spread.
limitations: Abstract-only review; no exact sample period, entry timing or magnitude should be inferred.
It does not prove symmetry for negative gaps or validate buying after two down days.
feature_hypotheses: Flag gap-up/attention-driven opening overextension and measure rebound already consumed before entry.

sources.title: Intraday Patterns in the Cross-Section of Stock Returns
sources.verified_content: Publisher-deposited abstract retrieved through Crossref; full text not obtained.
sources.sample: Not verified from accessible abstract; do not state a sample period.
sources.horizon: Half-hour intraday intervals, including lags at exact multiples of a trading day.
findings: Same-time-of-day return continuation persists across at least 40 trading days.
Very short reversal reflects temporary liquidity imbalances lasting less than one hour and bid-ask bounce.
limitations: Abstract-only review; cannot infer exact sample or replicable net trading profits.
Half-hour continuation and subhour reversal are different hypotheses from a two-day dip followed by full-session return.
feature_hypotheses: If future research uses opening-range confirmation, define a later entry and score its actual entry-to-close return.

sources.title: Opening and Closing Crosses
sources.section: Nasdaq Opening and Closing Cross Times; On-Open Orders; Imbalance Data
sources.verified_content: Official exchange HTML directly retrieved and inspected.
findings: Nasdaq states that the Opening Cross occurs at 9:30 a.m. Eastern.
On-open orders request execution at the opening price; indicative imbalance and likely price information is disseminated before the cross.
sources.inference: An entry rule conditioned on the final opening print is decided after that print is known, so a backtest cannot assume the same auction fill without an explicitly feasible pre-auction rule. Indicative auction price and final open are distinct.
feature_hypotheses: Use prior-close/pre-auction inputs for an auction-entry strategy, or observe the opening signal then test next-executable-price-to-close returns with timestamps and slippage.

sources.title: Opening and Closing Auctions
sources.section: Auction Timelines (All Eastern Times): NYSE Opening Auction; NYSE Arca Opening Auction
sources.verified_content: Official exchange HTML directly retrieved and inspected.
findings: NYSE’s opening-auction process starts at 9:30 a.m. Eastern; a particular security may be opened later by its DMM.
NYSE Arca specifies its core opening auction at 9:30 a.m., with an order freeze before the auction.
sources.inference: A generic 9:31/9:35 entry test must also confirm the individual security has actually opened; observing an official opening gap is not identical to participating in that opening auction.
